https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/ry.text: Ryanair passengers were fed-up after being stuck at a European airport for almost 15 hours. Around 150 people were left stranded at the gates of Krakow Airport after the Ryanair FR6359 service to Liverpool John Lennon Airport was delayed all day. Passengers were supposed to jet off at 8:55am local time on Monday morning (August 3) - but the flight only set off at 12:32am on Tuesday (August 4). The two-hour flight eventually touched down at 2am in Liverpool, 15 hours and 20 minutes later than scheduled. Ryanair said the delays were due to "a minor technical issue with the aircraft earlier today" requiring a replacement aircraft in an update to passengers, reports the Liverpool Echo. Marcin Tkaczyk, 47, from Lancaster, was one of the people who was left waiting in departures for hours. He said: "We're waiting next to the gate. We could leave, but then we'd have to go through the whole procedure again, and there is nothing around the airport so there's really no point. "People are upset. There's no one in person here to explain things to us. We were supposed to arrive in Liverpool at 10.40am [on Monday]. Now we don't know. If we do depart at 12:30am, it should be 3am [on Tuesday]." Flight updates sent to passengers read: "Your flight FR6359 from Krakow to Liverpool is delayed due to a minor technical issue with the aircraft earlier today. We organised a replacement aircraft to operate your flight, but this caused a delay." A further message read: "Since your flight has been delayed, please enjoy a snack or beverage on us by presenting your boarding pass to the cashier at participating outlets. We have issued one 17.00 PLN (Polish zloty) voucher per boarding pass in your booking. Please note refreshment vouchers cannot be redeemed onboard the aircraft." Marcin added: "The last we heard from Ryanair was about four or five hours ago. I'm fed up and upset. Fortunately we haven't got children with us, but there are a few kids here managing with phones, smartphones and Nintendos." In a statement to the Mirror, a spokesperson for Ryanair said passengers were given multiple options, including receiving a full refund and changing their flight free of charge. They were also offered five sets of vouchers, totalling 85PLN (£16.93). A spokesperson for the airline said: " “ This flight from Krakow to Liverpool (3 Aug) was delayed due to a technical issue with the aircraft. Passengers were notified and kept up-to-date via email, PUSH notifications and ground staff. "Passengers were offered to receive a full refund, to change flight free of charge, or to wait for this flight, which departed Krakow at 00:32am local time. Passengers who chose to wait for this flight received 5 sets of vouchers (85 PLN total)."

https://www.atvtoday.co.uk/317388-cultur.text: The 17th edition of Lithuania’s contemporary art fair will feature 70 galleries from more than 20 countries Vilnius will host the 17th edition of ArtVilnius from 1–4 October, bringing together 70 galleries from more than 20 countries. The contemporary art fair will take place at the Lithuanian Exhibition and Congress Centre Litexpo, with this year’s main exhibition examining the artistic connections between Vilnius, Warsaw and Vienna. The programme will explore the three European capitals through exhibitions, curated projects and discussions, looking at their shared histories alongside the different artistic directions emerging from each city. “Looking at Vilnius alongside Warsaw and Vienna allows us to step outside the familiar boundaries of our region,” says Neringa Bumblienė, Artistic Director and Curator of the Vilnius Performance Art Biennial. “It reveals unexpected connections and differences, and gives us a chance to see ourselves and our neighbours from a different perspective.” A central part of the fair will be The Path , ArtVilnius’ annual curated competition, which brings together artists from Lithuania and abroad. For the first time, the exhibition is being curated by Vienna-based artist, curator and writer Aliaksei Barysionak. Following an open call, Barysionak selected 11 artists from Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Belgium, Belarus and Ukraine. Their work explores themes including war, forced migration, ecological threats and social fragility, using sculpture, installation and performance. “I was surprised by how fragile, subtle and even gentle the exhibition became,” says Barysionak. “The artists work with everyday, industrial and infrastructural materials, yet they speak about very deep and painful things.” Among the works on display will be Deposit , a 1.3-metre-high sculpture by Estonian-UK artist Bob Bicknell-Knight, reflecting his interest in the relationship between digital and physical worlds. Lithuanian-Norwegian artist Kasparas Brazovskis will present the site-specific installation Fences vs. Bulldozer Tactics , which explores ideas around barriers, construction and urban space. Lithuanian sculptor Vytautas Viržbickas will contribute Džiaugsmai ( Joys ), a five-metre-wide sculpture made from black pipe fittings originally intended for a Russian water-treatment business. The international gallery programme will also include participants from Vienna. Christine König Galerie will present works by artists including Magda Csutak and Erwin Kneihsl. Csutak’s Quasi Meteorit combines wood, porcelain, iron, silicon dioxide and nickel oxide, while Kneihsl’s Ohne Titel (Sonne 58) combines silver gelatin photography and collage. The gallery’s presentation reflects its interest in areas including politics and activism, feminism, literature and post-conceptual art. Also taking part is Vienna-based Galerie Sturm & Schober, which will present artists including Swiss painter Dave Bopp. His mixed-media work Conjunction After Sunset combines layered abstract forms and shifting colours. ArtVilnius’26 will take place at Litexpo in Vilnius from 1–4 October 2026, with the wider programme combining gallery presentations with curated exhibitions, projects and discussions exploring contemporary art across the region.
